subject: Northstar Retail — runtime profile & model plan

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>

Subject: Northstar Retail — runtime profile & model plan

Hi Asha / Samir,

Following our kickoff yesterday, attaching a concise plan to get the model shortlist and workload sizing locked for the onboarding sprint. High level asks:

- Confirm primary inference surfaces (search re-rank, chat, and product-summary generation).
- Provide a realistic hourly request pattern for weekdays/weekends, and P95 peak concurrency if known.
- Share average and 90th-percentile prompt lengths (tokens) for each surface, or a sample of 200 requests if easier.

What we are proposing on the Redwood side (first-pass recommendations):
- Tier A (low-latency): quantized Llama 2 13B / RedQuant 13B for re-rank and chat with 8k context.
- Tier B (cost-optimized): 7B int8 variant for bulk product-summary generation where latency can be relaxed.
- Cache: prefix-KV cache for product-summary templates; 24-hour reuse window.

I attached a quick token workbook (northstar_token_estimates.xlsx) with placeholder hourly profiles — please replace the sample rows with your real traffic so we can size Dedicated capacity and autoscale windows.

Next steps: if you can drop the sample export by Tue (20th), Ben and I will run a workload projection and return a recommended pool sizing and expected per-1M-token cost. Also linking the living doc: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1nSg-northstar-onboard-plan

Thanks,
Marcus

--
Marcus Lin
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Northstar Retail — runtime profile & model plan

Hey Marcus / Marissa,

Thanks — we pulled together an export and a short note on usage patterns (see summary below). I attached the CSV sample and updated a few rows in your workbook. High level:

- Surfaces: 60% product-summary generation (background + on-demand), 30% search rerank, 10% chat/assist.
- Hourly profile (weekdays): baseline 350 req/hr, morning ramp to 2.2k/hr between 8–11am PT (our marketing emails drive spikes), sustained peak P95 concurrency ~70. Weekends baseline ~120 req/hr with smaller peaks.
- Token sizes: product-summary prompts avg 280 tokens, generation outputs avg 420 tokens (we included a sample). Search rerank requests are small: avg 45 tokens. Chat sessions vary; median prompt 220 tokens, but long sessions hit 2k tokens occasionally.

Questions:
1) For the chat long-session cases, will Redwood route to a higher-memory node automatically or do we need to cap context?
2) Any recommended fallback if Tier A capacity is saturated during marketing-driven spikes?

We placed Samir on this thread for infra + SLO questions.

Asha

Attachment: ns_sample_requests.csv (csv, 210 KB)
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-20T08:17:00-07:00
Subject: Internal: sizing quick take for Northstar

Internal note — quick sizing assumptions from the sample Asha sent:

- Baseline math (weekday): 350 req/hr -> ~8.4k req/day. With token mix, estimate ~28M input tokens/day and ~41M output tokens/day.
- Peak day: 2.2k/hr sustained for 3 hours -> add ~10M tokens during peak window.

Recommended first-pass configuration:
- Dedicated pool: 4 x A100p4-equivalent for Tier A (low-latency) with ability to burst to 6 for 3-hour marketing windows. This covers P95 latency targets of <220 ms for 13B quantized models with continuous batching.
- Tier B: 2 x T4-equivalent nodes running 7B int8 for background generation.
- Routing policy: route chat with session-length >1k tokens to Tier A only; short chat and rerank can use Tier B where possible.
- Autoscale policy: scheduled scale-up daily 07:30–11:30 PT and an on-call API to trigger emergency scale for marketing blasts.

I'll draft a brief mutual action plan and a cost ballpark. Marissa — can you check whether the customer wants a hard SLA for marketing spikes or prefers a managed fallback (degraded perf / cheaper model)?

-Ben

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Asha Patel <asha.patel@northstar.com>, Samir Rao <samir@northstar.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-21T16:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Northstar Retail — runtime profile & model plan

Thanks Asha — this is great and very actionable. Summary and agreed next steps below so everyone has a single source of truth: 

1) Model shortlist & routing
   - Tier A (low-latency): RedQuant Llama-13B (8k) — default for chat >1k tokens and rerank.
   - Tier B (cost-opt): 7B int8 variant for non-interactive product-summary generation and small chat snippets.

2) Capacity & autoscale
   - Initial Dedicated pool: 4 x A100p4-eq for Tier A, 2 x T4-eq for Tier B. Autoscale schedule: daily ramp 07:30–11:30 PT + manual on-call trigger for unscheduled blasts. Bursting to 6 nodes for up to 4 hours is acceptable per our pricing term draft.

3) Operational controls and fallback
   - Routing rule: route long chat sessions to Tier A. When Tier A is saturated, fallback to Tier B for non-session-critical rerank only; chat requests will return an explanatory 503 with suggested retry/backoff for long sessions (we can flip to degraded-mode vs hard error if you prefer).

4) Data we still need from your side
   - Finalized hourly CSV (you updated our workbook — we received it) and confirmation if marketing spikes are covered by hard SLA or managed fallback.

5) Deliverables / timeline
   - By 2027-04-23: Redwood will deliver a capacity-cost estimate and a one-page mutual action plan (I will attach model_shortlist_rationale.pdf).
   - By 2027-04-30: Target for first pilot with production sampling on Tier B for product-summary generation.

If that aligns, we'll convert this summary into the mutual action plan in HubSpot and schedule a 30-min sync to walk through the pool sizing. Proposed times: Thu 04/22 10:30 PT or Fri 04/23 09:00 PT.

Best,
Marcus
